newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end up 0.59 pct after profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end up 0.59 pct after profit taking.

text.p: Greek stocks closed up 0.59 percent on Wednesday on high volume after an intra-day correction with analysts saying the market might further correct this week but would eventually regain momentum.

"The market corrected during the session in profit taking after new scenarios about the banking sector. But it closed higher as a sign of a bullish market which is driven by easing inflation and interest rates," said Vassilis Kletsas at Telesis Securities.
Market talk wants Ionian Bank to be merging with Commercial Bank and National Bank to be considering policies on dividends and profits, creating some uncertainty in the market, he added.
Block trades of 9,000 shares of Alpha Credit at 20,200 drachmas and 10,000 shares of National Bank at 21,500 drachmas signalled increased activity in the banking sector.
Aluminium and cement shares were still superior performers, Kletsas said.
"The market came to an equilibrium on Wednesday, with demand meeting supply," said broker Dimitris Tsekouras, at Tsekouras Securities.
Intense buying, which pushed up the index on Tuesday, was met by selling interest on Wednesday, stabilising the market, he said.
He predicted a stable performance for the next few days, with the index fluctuating around Wednesday's levels.
The Athens general share index closed 0.59 percent or 6.82 points up at 1156.02 from Tuesday's 1149.20, after opening at 1150.31.
Banks gained 1.33 percent, construction rose 0.22 percent and investment shares ended 0.17 percent down. Small caps ended 0.86 percent down and industrials lost 0.85 percent.
Wednesday's turnover was 15.8 billion drachmas on volume of 4.9 million shares. Losers led gainers 132 to 80 with 26 issues unchanged on 238 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 881.00-899.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, did not change and closed at 5,300.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $20.79-$21.79. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 8,280-8,803 drachmas.
